Kongruentna su zglobna tijela.
Mrljaste zone crvene rekonverzije koštane srži u metadijafizi femura.
Hondromalacija patelarne hrskavice I-II°. Denudacija trohlearne hrskavice u medijalnom dijelu uz
manji fokus koštanog edema (hondromalacija IV°).
Stanjenje zglobnih hrskavica femorotibijalnog zgloba uz disekacijske promjene i hondromalaciju
III° medijalnog femoralnog kondila te lateralnog tibijalnog platoa. Rubna osteofitoza svih
zglobnih površina femorotibijalnog zgloba i FP zgloba.
Opisano odgovara srednje teškoj gonartrozi.
Minimalni zglobni izljev.
Prednji i stražnji križni ligamenti su primjerenog intenziteta signala, bez znakova rupture.
Septirana ganglijska cista uz stražnji križni ligament veličine 14x5mm na sagitalnim presjecima.
Lateralni mensik je izmjenjenog intenziteta signala u smislu miksoidne degeneracije uz vidljivu
kroničnu kompleksnu ruputuru korpusa na podlozi degenerativno promjenjenog meniska, koja
seže do tibijalne artikulacijske površine. Također kompleksna ruptura stražnjeg roga i korijena.
Ekstruzija korpusa lateralnog meniska van zglobne površine za do 3mm.
Vidljiv je defekt donjih popliteomeniscealnih fascikla uz formiranje ganglion ciste duž tetive
muskulusa popliteusa, na aksijalnim presjecima veličine 20 × 8 mm.
Medijalni menisk je izmjenjenog intenziteta signala u vidu miksoidne degeneracije, bez znakova
rupture. Manja eksturzija u području korpusa za do 2mm.
Medijalni kolateralni ligament je primjerenog intenziteta signala, bez znakova rupture.
Lateralni kolateralni ligament je smanjene napetosti uz izmjenjen intenzitet signala pri
femoralnom hvatištu, vjerojatno uslijed distenzije.
Manji izljev u ovojnici tetive m. popliteusa koja je izmjenjenog intenziteta signala pri femoralnom
hvatištu u sklopu tendinopatskih promjena.
U području insercije za tibiju manja parcijalna ruptura tetive muskulusa semimembranozusa.
Tetive pes anserinusa i iliotibijalni trakt su primjerenog intenziteta signala.
Tetiva m. kvadricepsa i ligg. patele su izmjenjenog intenzita signala u području hvatišta u smislu
entezopatskih promjena.
Neurovaskularne strukture su primjerenog prikaza.

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Clicking, locking, exclude meniscal tear..

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination. The extensor mechanism is intact. There is patella alta. The Insall Salvati ratio measures about 1.6.
The finding is associated with advanced patellofemoral joint osteoarthritic change with extensive denuding of the articular cartilage and with extensive subcortical cyst formation particularly seen along the apex and lateral facet of patella. Prominent trochlear and patellar osteophytes are demonstrated.

The medial patellar retinaculum is attenuated likely related to previous lateral dislocation and partial disruption. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact.

There is a degenerative medial meniscal tear. There is maceration and linear signal seen in the posterior horn extending into the body. An oblique inferiorly surfacing tear of the body and posterior horn is a demonstrated. The finding is associated with severe chondral denuding and exuberant marginal osteophyte formation seen to the medial joint compartment. There is also subcortical edema seen to the weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.

The lateral meniscus is macerated and not identified at the body and posterior horn. Findings are in keeping with extensive maceration and degenerative tearing of the body and the posterior horn of lateral meniscus. The finding is associated with denuding of the entire articular cartilage of lateral joint compartment associated with prominent lateral joint compartment osteophyte formation. There is also subcortical sclerosis and mild edema seen within the lateral joint compartment. An intraosseous cyst is seen to the lateral femoral condyle with 3 cm in keeping with subcortical tear.

The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate and medial collateral ligament are intact.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon appear intact.

There is a large knee effusion with reactive synovitis. There is no significant Baker's cyst. In the lateral popliteal fossa there is a large intraosseous loose body projecting anterior to the proximal fibers of the lateral head of the gastrocnemius measuring about 2.4 cm in maximum dimension. Smaller loose bodies are likely present in this region.

INTERPRETATION: 

Severe tricompartmental osteoarthritic change most severely affecting patellofemoral and lateral compartments. Degenerative meniscal tears laterally and medially with cartilaginous denuding to the lateral medial and patellofemoral compartments.

Loose bodies.

Patella alta with attenuation of the medial patellar retinaculum likely related to prior transient lateral dislocation of the patella.

COMPARISON:[Date].

CLINICAL HISTORY:One-year history right knee pain after blunt trauma to the anterior knee.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The medial meniscus is intact. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, as well as iliotibial band are intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. Minimal lateral patellar subluxation. There is edema within the superolateral aspect of the infrapatellar fat-pad, suggesting underlying lateral femoral condylar patellar tendon friction syndrome. This is new from previous study. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 11 mm, within normal limits.

There is mild to moderate patellofemoral chondrosis, new since previous study. Preserved medial and lateral femorotibial articular cartilage.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Progressive mild to moderate patellofemoral chondrosis suggesting evolving patellofemoral osteoarthritis.
2. Infrapatellar fat pad edema suggestive of underlying lateral femoral condylar patellar tendon friction syndrome.

Findings:  No evidence of knee effusion. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is minor irregularity of the weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle articular cartilage but no cartilage loss. Normal lateral tibiofemoral and patellofemoral articular cartilage.  A small ganglion formation is noted within the cranial aspect of the lateral gastrocnemius muscle head.  
Conclusion: No major abnormality is identified.

FINDINGS:

There is a large knee joint effusion with synovitis. There is no popliteal cysts.

There are severe degenerative changes in the lateral compartment with full-thickness cartilage loss at and subchondral reactive changes. There are moderate degenerative changes in the medial and patellofemoral compartments with high-grade cartilage thinning involving the lateral patellar facet and lateral aspect of femoral trochlea.

There is diffuse intrasubstance degeneration with maceration, extrusion and degenerative tearing of the lateral meniscus. The medial meniscus demonstrates intrasubstance degeneration without a well-defined linear tear.

There is intrasubstance mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

Otherwise the extensor mechanism, the medial collateral ligament, the pes anserine tendons, the semimembranosus, the popliteus, the distal biceps femoris, the lateral collateral ligament and the IT band are unremarkable.

CONCLUSION:

1. Moderate to severe degenerative changes most pronounced in the lateral compartment with areas of full-thickness cartilage loss as detailed above.

2. Diffuse intrasubstance degeneration with maceration and degenerative tearing of the lateral meniscus with intrasubstance degeneration of the medial meniscus. There is no well-defined linear tear.

3. Intrasubstance mucoid degeneration of the ACL without ligament injury.

4. Knee joint effusion with synovitis without popliteal cyst.

Zeer degeneratief voorkomen van de posterieure kruisband (onregelmatig, gestegen T2-signaal, verdund en dan weer verdikt). Beginnend lateraal femorotibiaal kraakbeenlijden, graad 2 . Beginnend femoropatellair kraakbeenlijden graad 2 met enkele oppervlakkige fissuren . [BILATERAL NOTE: report filed jointly for both studies]
The two studies are being reported together.  
Faint linear intrasubstance fluid hyperintensity is noted at the posterior horns of both menisci, in keeping with age-related persistent vascularity.  
Otherwise intact menisci, cruciate and collateral ligaments, popliteus musculotendinous units, extensor tendons and both distal iliotibial bands.  
No skeletal abnormalities of note. 
No patellofemoral dysplasia morphology demonstrated on either side.  
Well-maintained tricompartmental articular cartilage surfaces are appreciated bilaterally, with no osteochondral lesions being demonstrated.  
No knee joint effusions are present on either side, nor are there any intra-articular loose bodies. 
No anterior fat pad impingement has been demonstrated either.  
Grossly unremarkable imaged extra-articular soft tissues.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Sprain; medial left knee pain for 2 months, no known injury
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla extremity system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tear involving the body and posterior horn with horizontal and radial components, with mild extrusion and associated reactive bone marrow edema along the peripheral medial tibial plateau. No meniscal fragments. 
Medial compartment cartilage: Partial-thickness cartilage loss along the medial aspect of the medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 11 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Complex tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with mild extrusion.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Contusión rodilla derecha con dolor persistente lateral. Descartar edema óseo.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Aumento de señal , sugiriendo una rotura parcial de la unión entre el cuerno posterior y la raíz meniscal
posterior del menisco lateral, sin desplazamiento de segmentos ni extrusión meniscal.
Aumento de señal central del cuerno posterior y cuerpo del menisco medial que contacta la superficie
articular de manera periférica a nivel del cuerpo compatible una rotura, no desplazada. Discreto edema las
partes blandas regionales.
Úlceras condrales focales de espesor total lineales del platillo tibial lateral, sin cambios óseos simples.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial y total de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial sin cambios

condropatía superficial. Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial y prácticamente total de la unión de la faceta
medial con el vértice de la rótula.
No hay significativo derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Leve aumento de señal del tercio proximal del tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura. Cambios entesopáticos
cuadricipitales distales.
Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Signos de una rotura parcial de la unión entre cuerno posterior y la raíz meniscal posterior del menisco
lateral.
Signos de una rotura periférica del menisco medial.
Úlceras condrales focales grado 3 de platillo tibial lateral.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 y 3 del cóndilo femoral medial y de la rótula. Condropatía superficial de la
tróclea femoral.
Leve tendinosis rotuliana proximal.
Cambios entesopáticos cuadricipitales distales
